obligations: A generation service may not distribute a counterfeit intimate image without first obtaining consent from the identifiable individual depicted (Sec. 13-72b-201(2)).

To obtain consent sufficient to meet the requirements, a generation service shall implement and maintain a consent system that requires the identifiable individual to affirmatively provide consent before distribution, assures the identity of the individual with reasonable accuracy, and maintains a record of the consent for not less than seven years (Sec. 13-72b-201(3)).

A generation service may not require an individual to disclose personally identifiable information beyond what is reasonably necessary to assure the individual's identity and obtain valid consent (Sec. 13-72b-201(4)).

A generation service shall take reasonable measures to inform users that distribution of nonconsensual counterfeit intimate images is prohibited, violations may result in civil liability, and the service provides procedures for reporting violations (Sec. 13-72b-205(1)).
A generation service shall clearly and conspicuously provide to users procedures for reporting violations (Sec. 13-72b-205(2)).

A generation service shall publish in a clear and conspicuous location on its website or primary user interface the written policy required by Subsection 13-72b-203(1)(b) and a general description of safeguards implemented to prevent generation of nonconsensual counterfeit intimate images (Sec. 13-72b-205(3)).
A covered platform may not knowingly allow the distribution of a counterfeit intimate image without consent from the identifiable individual depicted (Sec. 13-72b-301(1)).
A covered platform shall establish and implement notice and removal procedures that comply with Section 3(a) of the Take It Down Act (Sec. 13-72b-302(1)).

The notice and removal procedures must include establishing a mechanism for an individual depicted to notify the platform, providing clear and conspicuous notice of the mechanism, removing the reported image within 48 hours after receiving notice, and making reasonable efforts to identify and remove any identical copy (Sec. 13-72b-302(2)).

A large online platform shall detect whether compliant system provenance data is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the platform, provide a user interface to disclose the availability of system provenance data, and allow a user to inspect all available compliant system provenance data in an easily accessible manner (Sec. 13-72c-201(1)).

A capture device manufacturer shall include a latent disclosure in content captured by the capture device that conveys the name of the capture device manufacturer or digital signatures sufficient to prove whether the content was created using a type of capture device, and the time and date of the content's creation or alteration (Sec. 13-72c-202(1)).
A capture device manufacturer may provide a user with the option to disable the latent disclosure (Sec. 13-72c-202(2)).

A capture device manufacturer shall comply with this section only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body (Sec. 13-72c-202(3)).

A covered provider shall include a latent disclosure in image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination of image, video, or audio, created or substantially modified by the covered provider's generative artificial intelligence system that meets the criteria in Sec. 13-72c-203 (Sec. 13-72c-203).

The chief information officer shall make rules establishing standards for digital content on a webpage of a state agency that the public can access to facilitate a transaction or obtain a service if the chief information officer determines there is a substantial risk that fraudulent or misleading media could cause harm to a resident of the state interacting with the state agency (Sec. 63A-16-215(1)).

The standards required by Subsection (1) shall require a digitally accessible provenance record containing provenance information for digital content captured, created, or edited that includes identification of the type of software or tool used or the specific tool used, the date of creation, a content identifier, and the previous content identifiers if applicable (Sec. 63A-16-215(2)).
prohibitions: A generation service may not distribute a counterfeit intimate image without first obtaining consent from the identifiable individual depicted (Sec. 13-72b-201(2)).

A generation service may not require an individual to disclose personally identifiable information beyond what is reasonably necessary to assure the individual's identity and obtain valid consent (Sec. 13-72b-201(4)).
A covered platform may not knowingly allow the distribution of a counterfeit intimate image without consent from the identifiable individual depicted (Sec. 13-72b-301(1)).

A large online platform may not, to the extent technically feasible, knowingly strip any system provenance data or digital signature that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body from content uploaded or distributed on the large online platform (Sec. 13-72c-201(2)).

key_definitions: Artificial intelligence technology: the same as that term is defined in Section 13-72-101 (Sec. 13-72b-101(1))

Consent: express permission, freely and voluntarily given by an identifiable individual, with full knowledge of the nature and purpose of the generation of an intimate image depicting the individual, where the consent is specific to the particular intimate image being generated, obtained before generation, and may be revoked at any time (Sec. 13-72b-101(2))
Counterfeit intimate image: a digital forgery as that term is defined in the Take It Down Act (Sec. 13-72b-101(3))
Covered platform: the same as that term is defined in Section 3 of the Take It Down Act, Public Law 119-12, 139 Stat. 59, codified at 47 U.S.C. 230 note (Sec. 13-72b-101(4))

Distribute: to sell, exhibit, display, publish, provide, give, provide access to, or otherwise transfer a counterfeit intimate image, with or without consideration, and includes generation by a generation service and subsequent provision to the user (Sec. 13-72b-101(5))
Generate: to create, produce, compose, materially edit, or facilitate the creation of an intimate image through the use of artificial intelligence technology (Sec. 13-72b-101(6))

Generation service: a person that operates, maintains, or provides an interactive computer service that enables users to generate intimate images, processes user image generation requests through servers or computing resources controlled by the service operator rather than solely on the user's local device, and distributes generated intimate images to users through the service (Sec. 13-72b-101(7))

Identifiable individual: an individual who is recognizable as an actual human individual by the human individual's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic, including a unique physical feature or other recognizable attribute (Sec. 13-72b-101(8))
Intimate image: an intimate visual depiction as those terms are defined in the Take It Down Act (Sec. 13-72b-101(10))

Reasonable expectation of privacy: an individual's expectation that the individual's body will not be viewed, recorded, or depicted in an intimate image without the individual's knowledge and consent, and that an intimate image of the individual will not be generated, created, distributed, or manipulated without the individual's knowledge and consent (Sec. 13-72b-101(11))
Artificial intelligence: a machine based system that makes predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments (Sec. 13-72c-101(1))

Capture device: a device that can record photographs, audio, or video content, including a video camera, a still photography camera, a mobile phone with a built in camera or microphone, or a voice recorder (Sec. 13-72c-101(2))
Capture device manufacturer: a person who produces a capture device for sale in the state, but does not include a person exclusively engaged in the assembly of a capture device (Sec. 13-72c-101(3))
Compliant system provenance data: system provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications of an established standards setting body (Sec. 13-72c-101(4))

Covered provider: a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system that has over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state, but does not include a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system used exclusively for the person's internal business operations and not made publicly accessible (Sec. 13-72c-101(5))
Digital signature: a cryptography based method that identifies the user or entity that attests to the information provided in the signed section (Sec. 13-72c-101(6))

Generative artificial intelligence system: an artificial intelligence system that can generate derived synthetic content, including text, images, video, or audio, that emulates the structure and characteristics of the system's training data (Sec. 13-72c-101(7))

Large online platform: a public facing social media platform, mass messaging platform, or stand alone search engine that distributes content to users who did not create or collaborate in creating the content and that exceeded 2,000,000 unique monthly users during the preceding 12 months, but does not include a broadband internet access service or a telecommunications service (Sec. 13-72c-101(8))

Manifest: easily perceived, understood, or recognized by a natural person (Sec. 13-72c-101(10))
Mass messaging platform: a direct messaging platform that allows users to distribute content to more than 100 users simultaneously (Sec. 13-72c-101(11))
Metadata: structural or descriptive information about data (Sec. 13-72c-101(12))
Personal information: the same as that term is defined in Section 13-61-101 (Sec. 13-72c-101(13))

Provenance data: data that is embedded into digital content, or that is included in the digital content's metadata, for the purpose of verifying the digital content's authenticity, origin, or history of modification (Sec. 13-72c-101(14))

User: a Utah resident who accesses, interacts with, or uses an interactive computer service, platform, generation service, generative artificial intelligence system, or capture device (Sec. 13-72c-101(16))
User interface: the method by which an individual interacts with, controls, or receives information from a computer, software application, website, or electronic device (Sec. 13-72c-101(17))
compliance_steps: Determine whether the organisation is a generation service, covered platform, large online platform, capture device manufacturer, or covered provider under the definitions (Sec. 13-72b-101, Sec. 13-72c-101).

If a generation service, implement a consent system that obtains affirmative consent from depicted individuals before distributing counterfeit intimate images, verifies identity with reasonable accuracy, and keeps records for at least seven years (Sec. 13-72b-201(3)).

Adopt and publish a written policy prohibiting nonconsensual counterfeit intimate images, with reasonable safeguards and reporting procedures, and inform users of prohibitions and reporting mechanisms (Sec. 13-72b-203(1)(b), Sec. 13-72b-205).

If a covered platform, establish notice and removal procedures compliant with the Take It Down Act, including a notification mechanism, clear notice, removal within 48 hours, and efforts to remove identical copies (Sec. 13-72b-302).

If a large online platform, implement detection of compliant system provenance data, provide a user interface to disclose and allow inspection of that data, and avoid stripping compliant provenance data or digital signatures (Sec. 13-72c-201).

If a covered provider, include latent disclosures in AI generated or substantially modified image, video, or audio content that convey time and date and either capture device manufacturer name or digital signatures proving AI creation, consistent with industry standards (Sec. 13-72c-203).

If a capture device manufacturer, include latent disclosure in captured content conveying manufacturer name or digital signatures and time and date, with option to disable, for devices produced for sale on or after January 1, 2028 (Sec. 13-72c-202).
Monitor for notices of violations and respond promptly to prevent further distribution or remove content (Sec. 13-72b-203(1)(g), Sec. 13-72b-302(2)(c)).
For state agencies, follow rules from the chief information officer on provenance records for public webpages if substantial risk (Sec. 63A-16-215).

notable_exemptions: A generation service that has implemented and maintains a written policy and reasonable technical safeguards that categorically prevent the generation of intimate images is not required to comply with certain consent requirements to qualify for safe harbor protection (Sec. 13-72b-203(3)).

A generation service qualifies for safe harbor if it meets conditions including no actual knowledge before notice, consent system operating as designed, reasonable reliance on consent system information, and prompt action upon discovering violation (Sec. 13-72b-203(2)).
A covered platform is not liable if it implemented and maintained compliant notice and removal procedures and acted in good faith in responding to notices (Sec. 13-72b-304(1)).

A covered platform qualifies for safe harbor even if a nonconsensual counterfeit intimate image appeared if it had no actual knowledge before notice and complied with takedown requirements after notice (Sec. 13-72b-304(2)).

Covered provider does not include a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system used exclusively for the person's internal business operations and not made publicly accessible (Sec. 13-72c-101(5)(b)).
Large online platform does not include a broadband internet access service or a telecommunications service (Sec. 13-72c-101(8)(b)).
Capture device manufacturer does not include a person exclusively engaged in the assembly of a capture device (Sec. 13-72c-101(3)(b)).
A capture device manufacturer may provide a user with the option to disable the latent disclosure (Sec. 13-72c-202(2)).
Section 63A-16-215 does not apply to digital content created before January 1, 2027 (Sec. 63A-16-215(3)).

This part does not expand or modify the notice and takedown requirements established in the Take It Down Act, and does not alter, modify, or limit Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act (Sec. 13-72b-306).

Actual damages need not be alleged or proved (Sec. 13-72b-202(3), Sec. 13-72b-303(3)). A plaintiff may recover actual damages including emotional distress, punitive damages if the violation is willful, reckless, or malicious, and reasonable attorney fees and costs (Sec. 13-72b-202(4), Sec. 13-72b-303(4)).   • A generation service should implement a written policy, reasonable safeguards, a consent system, and reporting procedures to qualify for safe harbor and avoid civil liability (Sec. 13-72b-203, Sec. 13-72b-205).
  • A covered platform must implement notice and takedown procedures, remove reported counterfeit intimate images within 48 hours, and make reasonable efforts to remove identical copies (Sec. 13-72b-302).
  • A large online platform must detect compliant system provenance data in distributed content, disclose its availability, allow users to inspect it, and not strip compliant provenance data or digital signatures (Sec. 13-72c-201).
  • A covered provider of a generative artificial intelligence system with over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and publicly accessible in Utah must include latent disclosures in AI generated or substantially modified image, video, or audio content conveying time and date and either capture device manufacturer name or digital signatures proving AI creation (Sec. 13-72c-203).
  • A capture device manufacturer must include latent disclosure in captured content starting January 1, 2028, with an option for users to disable it (Sec. 13-72c-202).
  • State agencies may need to follow provenance record standards for public webpages if the chief information officer determines substantial risk of fraudulent or misleading media (Sec. 63A-16-215).

Notable exemptions

  • A generation service that has implemented and maintains a written policy and reasonable technical safeguards that categorically prevent the generation of intimate images is not required to comply with certain consent requirements to qualify for safe harbor protection (Sec. 13-72b-203(3)).
  • A generation service qualifies for safe harbor if it meets conditions including no actual knowledge before notice, consent system operating as designed, reasonable reliance on consent system information, and prompt action upon discovering violation (Sec. 13-72b-203(2)).
  • A covered platform is not liable if it implemented and maintained compliant notice and removal procedures and acted in good faith in responding to notices (Sec. 13-72b-304(1)).
  • A covered platform qualifies for safe harbor even if a nonconsensual counterfeit intimate image appeared if it had no actual knowledge before notice and complied with takedown requirements after notice (Sec. 13-72b-304(2)).
  • Covered provider does not include a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system used exclusively for the person's internal business operations and not made publicly accessible (Sec. 13-72c-101(5)(b)).
  • Large online platform does not include a broadband internet access service or a telecommunications service (Sec. 13-72c-101(8)(b)).
  • Capture device manufacturer does not include a person exclusively engaged in the assembly of a capture device (Sec. 13-72c-101(3)(b)).
  • A capture device manufacturer may provide a user with the option to disable the latent disclosure (Sec. 13-72c-202(2)).
  • Section 63A-16-215 does not apply to digital content created before January 1, 2027 (Sec. 63A-16-215(3)).
  • This part does not expand or modify the notice and takedown requirements established in the Take It Down Act, and does not alter, modify, or limit Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act (Sec. 13-72b-306).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organisation is a generation service, covered platform, large online platform, capture device manufacturer, or covered provider under the definitions (Sec. 13-72b-101, Sec. 13-72c-101).
  • If a generation service, implement a consent system that obtains affirmative consent from depicted individuals before distributing counterfeit intimate images, verifies identity with reasonable accuracy, and keeps records for at least seven years (Sec. 13-72b-201(3)).
  • Adopt and publish a written policy prohibiting nonconsensual counterfeit intimate images, with reasonable safeguards and reporting procedures, and inform users of prohibitions and reporting mechanisms (Sec. 13-72b-203(1)(b), Sec. 13-72b-205).
  • If a covered platform, establish notice and removal procedures compliant with the Take It Down Act, including a notification mechanism, clear notice, removal within 48 hours, and efforts to remove identical copies (Sec. 13-72b-302).
  • If a large online platform, implement detection of compliant system provenance data, provide a user interface to disclose and allow inspection of that data, and avoid stripping compliant provenance data or digital signatures (Sec. 13-72c-201).
  • If a covered provider, include latent disclosures in AI generated or substantially modified image, video, or audio content that convey time and date and either capture device manufacturer name or digital signatures proving AI creation, consistent with industry standards (Sec. 13-72c-203).
  • If a capture device manufacturer, include latent disclosure in captured content conveying manufacturer name or digital signatures and time and date, with option to disable, for devices produced for sale on or after January 1, 2028 (Sec. 13-72c-202).
  • Monitor for notices of violations and respond promptly to prevent further distribution or remove content (Sec. 13-72b-203(1)(g), Sec. 13-72b-302(2)(c)).
  • For state agencies, follow rules from the chief information officer on provenance records for public webpages if substantial risk (Sec. 63A-16-215).
